says: In next/, with Q9/Q12 now held inside one hour, no law covers a refused send whose span ends in a new hour. There, the refusal adds one zero-byte write to the program's local quota account (writes 15 to 16, bytes and every table's row count unchanged). Whether a refusal may be charged that write is not decided anywhere the review found.
proof: Reviewer scratch copy of the pre-fix law, with the real Date.now set 3 ms before an hour at refusal 0: red at refusal 1, 'expected { program: { writes: 16 } } to deeply equal { program: { writes: 15 } }'. Debug output: table counts the same before and after, local program {writes:16,bytes:934} against {writes:15,bytes:934}.
cost: If charging a refused send a write when the hour turns is wrong, nothing now catches it, and a program near its write limit could lose a write to refusals.
